rationale: This is a mechanical rank-blend of two already-evaluated archive signals (the R&D-stock × clean-accrual corner and the goodwill-flow × dirty-accrual corner from BuyVsBuildAccrualFinanced / AcquiredIntangibleAccrualFlow), so it tests ensembling rather than a new economic mechanism and its alpha will be a near-deterministic average of results already known.

A defensible reframing of the buy-vs-build family that swaps the acquisition *flow* (asset-growth-contaminated) for a balance-sheet *stock* composition, though it overlaps materially with BuyVsBuildAccrualFinanced and the raw difference of two differently-scaled ratios before ranking is a crude composition measure.

The expression correctly isolates the working-capital component of the wedge (ib − oancf + dp ≈ ΔWC less other non-cash items) and the sign logic is internally consistent, but it is a component decomposition of the archive's best specification that partially duplicates InnovationWorkingCapitalDiscipline and reverts to essentially the canonical Sloan accrual definition.

Internally inconsistent: for a clean firm with ib = oancf the expression still equals ib·R/(ceq(ceq+R)) > 0, so profitable, cash-backed, R&D-heavy firms — precisely the population the archive finds *underpriced* — land at the short extreme, meaning the mechanical hidden-capital term fights the stated accrual story and the expected negative sign.

A legitimate and clearly falsifiable attribution test of whether the acquisition-accrual result is distinct from the asset-growth anomaly, with the caveat that a rank difference is not real orthogonalization and the embedded low-asset-growth tilt pushes against the expected negative sign, biasing the test toward rejection.

Despite the disclaimer, MUL(RANK(NEG(trend)), RANK(accrual)) ≈ (1−a)(1−b) is the mirror corner of SustainedRnDRampCleanAccruals' ab and is negatively correlated with it, so with a negative expected sign this is effectively a sign-flipped restatement of an already-tested, weak-alpha signal.
